title: Advocates Act, 1961 — Section 30 (Right of advocates to practise)

content.overview: Section 30 gives an advocate whose name is on a State roll the right to practise throughout India in all courts including the Supreme Court, and before tribunals and authorities.
content.glance: Section 30 gives an advocate whose name is on a State roll the right to practise throughout India in all courts including the Supreme Court, and before tribunals and authorities.
content.study: Subject to the Act, every advocate whose name is entered in the State roll is entitled as of right to practise throughout the territories to which the Act extends, in all courts including the Supreme Court, and before any tribunal or person legally authorised to take evidence, and before any other authority or person before whom such advocate is entitled to practise.

sections.heading: Operative rule
sections.body: Section 30 gives an advocate whose name is on a State roll the right to practise throughout India in all courts including the Supreme Court, and before tribunals and authorities.
